Reason: Figure 1 shows a small left pleural effusion and dense retrocardiac opacity, while Figure 2 (representing a later timepoint in this clinical sequence) demonstrates complete resolution of the effusion but persistence of the retrocardiac density; this dissociation suggests the opacity is a chronic underlying pathology rather than an acute infectious consolidation that would typically resolve with the effusion. *(guided by t000001)*
